name: BullMQ
description: Typed BullMQ job queues with workers, scheduler, Redis fallback to in-process sync execution, optional Bull Board dashboard, and per-queue routing. Designed for background processing (image generation, email, webhooks, exports) where tasks are too slow for request/response cycles.
checklist: Install dependencies: npm install bullmq ioredis (and @bull-board/nextjs @bull-board/api if bull_board=true)
Start Redis locally: redis-server (or `docker compose up redis` if you also installed the docker template)
If BULLMQ_FALLBACK_MODE=auto, the app works without Redis — watch for [bullmq:fallback] warnings in the console
Same-process mode: server/startup/start-workers.ts is imported at server startup — wire it into your Next.js custom server or instrumentation hook
Separate-service mode: run `node --import tsx/esm scripts/start-worker.ts` on a worker dyno/machine; same-process startup file is still emitted but should not be imported
Visit http://localhost:3000/admin/queues for Bull Board (if enabled). Set BULL_BOARD_USERNAME/PASSWORD before production
Add jobs via `addJob('<queue>', '<jobName>', data)` from src/infrastructure/queue; routes by job.name to the handler in src/infrastructure/queue/jobs/
Recurring jobs: edit src/infrastructure/queue/scheduler/job-scheduler.ts — definitions stay in code, stale ones are removed on next startup
